sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's fromJust on Nothing causes a runtime crash — demanding certainty from absence is fatal
sketches.resonance: Insisting on extracting something from nothing destroys everything, the way demanding answers from silence breaks what was left.
sketches.draft:
import Data.Maybe

whatYouPromised :: Maybe a
whatYouPromised = Nothing

main = print (fromJust whatYouPromised)

sketches.mechanism: A WeakReference becomes None once the referent is garbage collected — the reference exists but the thing it points to has already disappeared
sketches.resonance: You can hold a reference to someone who is already gone; the language lets you keep pointing at what no longer exists.
sketches.draft:
import weakref

class You:
    pass

you = You()
remembering = weakref.ref(you)
del you

print(remembering())

sketches.mechanism: method_missing is called when you invoke a method that doesn't exist — the object responds to everything by admitting it has no answer
sketches.resonance: Asked anything at all, grief can only repeat that it doesn't know how to do what you need.
sketches.draft:
class Grief
  def method_missing(what_you_need, *_)
    method_missing(what_you_need)
  end
end

Grief.new.move_on
